incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 pager triggered — elevated packet loss and DNS path divergence observed for eu-west region egress. Autopage to #incidents and on-call.
Alex: saw the pager, investigating now. impacted services: api-edge-eu, file-upload-proxy.
Priya: I can confirm — BGP updates from TransitProviderX are flapping on our primary egress pair in eu-west-1. We're seeing ~12-18% packet loss to a subset of downstream prefixes.
Matt: adding context — Cloud provider's internal routing seems fine, this looks like upstream route churn. DNS lookups for some customers are resolving via alternate AS paths that are returning higher latency.
Nina: is this affecting cross-region replication or just external egress?
Alex: primarily external customer traffic. Cross-region replication to us-east has increased latency but not failed.
Priya: capturing a quick dump: `show ip bgp neighbors` shows repeated Prefix RIB withdraws from TransitProviderX at .345s intervals.
Matt: can we temporarily de-preference that peer via BGP community or local-pref?
Alex: yes, I'm pushing a temporary local-pref to bias traffic to TransitProviderY for affected prefixes. Doing a canary on 10 prefixes first.
Priya: confirmed — after local-pref change, packet loss for the test prefixes dropped to 1-2%.
Ben: CS reporting a handful of customers with 503s for uploads in eu-west, starting ~1838012000. Can we estimate % of traffic impacted?
Matt: rough numbers: ~0.9% of total egress requests in eu-west, but concentrated on large object uploads -> heavier impact for a smaller number of customers.
Alex: paging note: we've opened ticket TPX-9876 with TransitProviderX and tagged as P1. They acknowledged and are investigating a mis-advertised aggregate.
Priya: collecting pcap + flow logs. attaching sample (s3 link): https://redwood-internal/snapshots/1838012345/pcap.gz
Nina: handoff — I'm taking primary oncall at 1838012500. Alex, can you summarize current mitigation and needed follow-ups?
Alex: handoff summary: (1) temporary local-pref applied to favor TransitProviderY for affected prefixes, (2) canary verification succeeded for 10 prefixes, (3) TPX ticket opened, (4) flow captures uploaded, (5) CS pre-notified impacted customers. Need: keep monitoring for 2h, coordinate with TPX for full withdraw/reannounce, consider permanent community tweak if instability continues.
Nina: got it — I'll keep the canary running and widen to all prefixes after 10m if stable.
Matt: adding a health-check snippet we used: ```
# quick script
for pfx in $(cat pfxs.txt); do ping -c 5 $pfx || echo "bad $pfx"; done
```
Priya: note — DNS traces show some resolvers cached a path that now points at the old AS. TTLs are short but some caches still hit for ~90s. That explains residual errors.
Ben: CS updated customers: we flagged impacted tenants and offered workaround to reroute uploads via us-east temporarily. They asked for ETA.
Alex: ETA depends on TPX fix; if they can stop flapping within 30-45m we keep local-pref until after stabilization. If not, we'll keep the bias and file RFC for community tagging.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: incident_id=INC-2026-183801 — priority=SEV2 — status=investigating — responders=[Alex, Priya, Matt, Nina]
Nina: widening canary now to full prefix list. Monitoring dashboards: egress packet loss, BGP withdraws, DNS failed queries.
Matt: if we see withdraw rate drop below 1/min and packet loss <2% for 15m, mark mitigated.
Priya: TPX responded: 'We're pushing a global withdraw for the affected aggregate and will reannounce with corrected next-hops within 10m'.
Alex: good — I'll keep the local-pref active until TPX confirms reannounce.
Ben: CS — we sent a short status update to impacted customers, included mitigation steps and estimated 30–60m timeline.
Nina: logging next steps for post-incident: 1) provider RCA request, 2) consider BGP community policy to avoid single-peer dependency, 3) refine pagerthresholds for DNS path divergence, 4) update runbook with the `local-pref canary` play.
Matt: quick note: remember to check our prefix aggregation; avoid leaking more-specifics in case TPX accidentally prefers them.
Priya: capture snapshot at 1838012590 attached.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Status update: TPX reannounce complete. Observed withdraws decay, packet loss trending to baseline. Marking as partial mitigation — continue monitoring.
Alex: thanks — I'll stay on watch for 15 more minutes then hand to Nina for close.
Nina: taking 15m watch. If stable, will close and start postmortem doc.
Ben: CS will wait until full close before sending final customer note.
Alex: quick postmortem seeds: timeline (detection -> pager -> local-pref canary -> TPX withdraw/reannounce), impact (0.9% of egress, several tenants with upload failures), mitigation (temporary local-pref -> TPX fix), action-items (RCA, community policy, runbook update).
Nina: closing note: if anything changes ping @nina directly. thanks team. :thumbsup:
